messages:
elaine (sales): Heads-up: acme POC getting mixed 403/401s when calling /v1/generate and sometimes 'insufficient_scope'. They got keys from our console yesterday. Can eng triage?
shane (sales-eng): can you paste the failing request/response? short snippet is fine.
elaine (sales): here's what they sent:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-ALPHA123' \ 
  -H 'X-Org-Id: acme-prod' \ 
  -H 'X-Project-Id: project-42' \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","input":"test"}'
```
response 1:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"code":403,"message":"org id mismatch: token_org=acme-staging request_org=acme-prod"}}
```
response 2 (later):
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":{"code":401,"message":"invalid_scope: token missing scope: generation.write"}}
```
elaine (sales): they say sometimes removing X-Project-Id helps but not always.
shane (sales-eng): two separate failure modes: org binding mismatch and missing scopes. Maria, can you check token metadata for sk-test-ALPHA123?
maria (eng-oncall): @devops-bot get-token-meta sk-test-ALPHA123
devops-bot: lookup result for token sk-test-ALPHA123:
```
created_by=elaine scope_ids=[generation.read] bound_org=acme-staging bound_project=proj-staging
last_used=2026-06-05T18:12:10Z
```
maria (eng-oncall): token only has generation.read and is bound to acme-staging/proj-staging. If the client sets X-Org-Id to acme-prod we reject. Also write scope is missing so the write call fails with 401/insufficient_scope.
shane (sales-eng): that matches. Likely they provisioned a read-only demo token into prod env by accident. Two remediations: 1) provision correct prod token with generation.write and bound to acme-prod/proj-42, or 2) remove explicit org/project headers and let the token's binding be authoritative (but their proxy requires headers).
elaine (sales): customer wants a short-term fix so their CI job can demo end-to-end tonight. Can we create a time-limited token with prod/project scope and write permissions?
maria (eng-oncall): we can. I'll issue a timeboxed token for the demo: sk-temp-PRODWRITE expires in 3 hours, scopes=[generation.read,generation.write], bound_org=acme-prod bound_project=project-42. I'll post it in the secure channel. Also note: if they intend to use a single token across multiple projects we need a different entitlements flow.
shane (sales-eng): also saw a spike of 429s in the audit log earlier during their ramp test. Devops bot, show recent rate events for that token (last 20m).
devops-bot: rate events for sk-test-ALPHA123:
2026-06-05T18:11:30Z RATE_LIMIT token=sk-test-ALPHA123 reqs=180 window=60s limit=150
2026-06-05T18:11:58Z RATE_LIMIT token=sk-test-ALPHA123 reqs=210 window=60s limit=150

maria (eng-oncall): they were over the default demo rate limit. For tonight I can temporarily bump their demo quota to 400rps for 1 hour. That will reduce 429s but they still saw occasional 503s because their concurrency exceeded backend slots. If they want consistent large loads we should recommend Dedicated capacity.
elaine (sales): please apply the bump for tonight's demo at 19:00 PT. Also issue the temp token and send it to the customer's secure channel.
maria (eng-oncall): done: quota bumped to 400rps for 1h starting 2026-06-05T19:00Z. Temp token sk-temp-PRODWRITE created and shared securely (expires in 3h).
elaine (sales): customer verified: generate now returns 200. They ran a short script hitting 350rps and saw stable responses. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
shane (sales-eng): follow-up action: update presales checklist to verify token scopes (generation.write) and org/project bindings before demos. Add note about proxies that add headers.
elaine (sales): I'll close the POC support ticket and include lessons learned.
